newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic "disappointed" by FCC ruling.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic "disappointed" by FCC ruling.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp on Wednesday said they are "disappointed" by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission's ruling mandating lower access charges, and questioned the justification for the ruling.

"We are...disappointed that the FCC has gone beyond the requirements of the Telecom Act by mandating lower access charges rather than letting the market drive down prices," the firms said in a joint statement.
"We fail to see how the FCC's access charge rate reductions are justified, and we will read the full order to determine the impact on all of our customers," they said.

The FCC ruling, which stems from last year's communications law, called for a $1.7 billion reduction in annual charges long-distance carriers pay local companies to access their networks. Further it calls for a cut in access charges by a total of $18.5 billion over the next five years.
Bell Atlantic and NYNEX said they felt that the FCC has moved in the right direction by setting a flat charge rather than a per minute charge to cover the fixed costs of providing access service.
"The FCC has recognized our concerns and moderated the flat rate changes in charges for business customers," they said.
The firms voiced guarded support for the FCC's funding plans for universal service, or affordable phone service for all residents.

"Based on what we know now, we generally support the direction taken by the FCC on Universal Service funding, but we remain concerned that several commissioners stated an intent to move to a much larger fund," the firms said.
"The Universal Service fund is sufficient to meet the objectives of the Telecom Act," they added.
